affiliations: Ocean University of China, Ocean University of China, Ocean University of China, Guangzhou University, Qingdao Institute of Technology, Ocean University of China, Bangladesh Fisheries Research Institute, Ocean University of China, Ocean University of China and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Comprehensive Benefit Evaluation and Obstacle Factor Analysis of China's Offshore Aquaculture
detail.abstract: This study aims to quantitatively evaluate the comprehensive benefits of China's offshore aquaculture from 2008 to 2022 and conduct an in-depth analysis of its development obstacles. To this end, we constructed a comprehensive benefit evaluation indicator system covering ecological, social, and economic dimensions, and employed the CRITIC weighting method, a multi-index comprehensive evaluation model, the Pearson correlation coefficient, and an obstacle degree model for measurement and analysis. The main findings are as follows: During the study period, the comprehensive benefits of the offshore aquaculture industry showed a significant upward trend, experiencing three stages of evolution: "fluctuant exploration → steady recovery → accelerated growth", with recent growth primarily driven by social and economic benefits. Correlation analysis further revealed a significant strong positive correlation between the social benefit index and the economic benefit index (r ≈ 0.815), forming a mutually reinforcing synergistic enhancement mechanism. However, the ecological benefit index showed only a weak correlation with the social benefit index and an extremely weak correlation with the economic benefit index, indicating that the current economic growth and social welfare improvement of the industry mainly rely on capital investment and scale expansion, and are relatively "decoupled" from the process of ecological environment improvement. The obstacle factor analysis results indicate that low production efficiency per unit water volume is the primary bottleneck restricting benefit improvement; wastewater discharge from direct-discharge pollution sources is the main ecological constraint; simultaneously, there are capacity shortcomings in supervision and technological support systems. Based on these findings, this paper proposes that future policies should focus on implementing precision management based on ecological carrying capacity, strengthening whole-chain technological support and coordinated pollution prevention and control, and promoting industrial integration and innovation, to foster high-quality, sustainable, and resilient development of offshore aquaculture.

title: The Impact of Organizational Characteristics on Talent Attraction in Enterprises: Focusing on the New Energy Vehicle Industry
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Pukyong National University

detail.title: The Impact of Organizational Characteristics on Talent Attraction in Enterprises: Focusing on the New Energy Vehicle Industry
detail.abstract: This study investigates how organizational characteristics shape talent attractiveness in the new energy vehicle (NEV) industry. Drawing on tool-symbol theory, person–organization fit theory, and trait activation theory, we develop and test an integrated framework using survey data and structural equation modeling. The results show that compensation, organizational reputation, and career development opportunities exert the strongest positive effects on talent attractiveness. Organizational identification and job satisfaction partially mediate these relationships, while geographical location strengthens them. This study contributes to the talent attraction literature by uncovering underlying mechanisms and offers managerial implications for firms in emerging industries.

title: A lithium battery health state estimation approach based on SHAP-guided feature fusion and a diffusion model
affiliations: Shanghai Polytechnic University, Yancheng Institute of Technology, Shanghai Polytechnic University, Shanghai Polytechnic University, Shanghai Polytechnic University, Drexel University and Shanghai Polytechnic University

detail.title: A lithium battery health state estimation approach based on SHAP-guided feature fusion and a diffusion model
detail.abstract: Accurate and interpretable estimation of lithium-ion battery state of health (SOH) is essential for ensuring the safety and reliability of energy storage systems. However, existing data-driven approaches often suffer from degraded performance under small-sample conditions and provide limited insight into how predictions are made when processing raw sensor signals. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel end-to-end SOH estimation framework that synergistically combines a hybrid iTransformer–BiGRU architecture, diffusion-based data augmentation, and SHAP-guided interpretability analysis. The model takes raw voltage, current, and temperature time-series sequences as direct input, bypassing manual feature engineering. The iTransformer module captures long-range temporal correlations across cycles, while the BiGRU network models local degradation dynamics within each cycle, enabling comprehensive representation learning. To mitigate severe data scarcity—especially in batteries with few aging cycles—a denoising diffusion probabilistic model is employed to synthesize realistic multivariate time-series trajectories, effectively expanding the training set while preserving underlying degradation patterns. The Kepler Optimization Algorithm (KOA) is further integrated to automatically tune key hyperparameters of the prediction network for optimal performance. To enhance transparency, Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) are applied post-hoc to the trained model, quantifying the contribution of individual time steps and sensor channels to the final SOH prediction. This provides actionable insights into which segments of the charge/discharge profile (e.g., constant-current phase, relaxation period) are most informative for health assessment. Experimental validation on the NASA battery dataset demonstrates that the proposed method achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0014 (i.e., 0.14% of nominal capacity) and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.0018, outperforming several state-of-the-art benchmarks. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of both diffusion-based augmentation and the iTransformer–BiGRU backbone, while SHAP analysis reveals consistent attention to physically plausible degradation signatures. This work thus delivers a high-accuracy, data-efficient, and inherently interpretable solution for real-world battery health monitoring—even when only raw sensor data and limited cycling history are available.

title: Socioeconomic and Political Pathways to Achieving Environmental Sustainability in China
affiliations: Bahauddin Zakariya University

detail.title: Socioeconomic and Political Pathways to Achieving Environmental Sustainability in China
detail.abstract: The emphasis on environmental sustainability outcomes (ESO) in emerging economies has increased recently, requiring in-depth research to manage the complex interplay between socio-economic and sociopolitical factors. With a particular focus on China, this study describes this significant relationship using a good technique that comprises standardized questionnaires administered to a large sample of different organizational levels. This research examined several factors and their effects on ESO. First, the results show that the kind of economic system (EST) directly affects ESO; no direct relationship was discovered between ESO and the industrialization level (LI). Furthermore, it was demonstrated that government funding for eco-sustainability projects (GFESP) and community engagement and eco-education initiatives (CEEEI) had a direct impact on ESO.  Secondly, the results demonstrated that implementing eco-policies and regulations (IEPR) had a full mediating effect between EST and ESO. Third, political instability (PI) and corruption level (CL), which are essentially the outcome of China's current political and environmental issues, diminish the correlation between EST and ESO. These findings demonstrate that China's environmental sustainability has to be improved using a multimodal approach. The public is encouraged to push legislators to bolster eco-laws and policies in order to emphasize environmental preservation. Initiatives to reduce corruption and maintain political stability may also bolster the beneficial effects of economic frameworks on ESO.

title: Boundary neuron method for solving partial differential equations
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Texas State University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Boundary neuron method for solving partial differential equations
detail.abstract: We propose a boundary neuron method with random features (BNM-RF) for solving partial differential equations. The method approximates the unknown boundary function by a shallow network within the boundary integral formulation. With randomly sampled and fixed hidden parameters, the computation reduces to a linear least squares problem for the output coefficients, which avoids gradient based nonconvex optimization. This construction retains the dimensionality reduction of boundary integral equations and the linear solution structure of the random feature method. For elliptic problems, we establish convergence analysis by combining kernel-based method with random feature approximation, and obtain error bounds on both the boundary and the interior solution. Numerical experiments on Laplace and Helmholtz problems, including interior and exterior cases, show that the proposed method achieves competitive accuracy relative to the boundary element method and favorable performance relative to boundary integral neural networks in the tested settings with only few neurons. Overall, the proposed method provides a practical framework for combining boundary integral equations with neural network for problems on complex geometries and unbounded domains.

title: Evolution Characteristics and Prediction Analysis of Runoff in Middle and Lower Reaches of Yellow River
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Anhui Agricultural University, Guizhou Institute of Technology, Anhui Agricultural University, Nanjing Hydraulic Research Institute and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Evolution Characteristics and Prediction Analysis of Runoff in Middle and Lower Reaches of Yellow River
detail.abstract: Water disasters with uncertainties are an important factor restricting the economic development of ecologically fragile areas. Although clarifying the evolution laws of runoff in a mainstream is theoretically effective for interpreting prediction results, few related efforts have been implemented. This study adopted multiple statistical methods to analyze the evolution characteristics of runoff of three typical stations in the middle and lower reaches of the Yellow River of China, which represent different geographical and flow patterns. On this basis, the hydrological indicators at the three stations and environmental factors, such as soil moisture content, were utilized as input variables to predict the changing trend of runoff. The daily monitoring data from 2009 to 2022 was split into three parts to train, validate, and test the model at a ratio of 6:2:2. A hybrid prediction model BC-BiLSTM composed of the convolutional neural network (CNN) and bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) with the Bayesian optimization (BO) was proposed to deal with long time series runoff samples with various forms of variation. Compared with other models, the BC-BiLSTM performed better in terms of evaluation criteria of MSE, MAE, and R2. The annual runoff showed an overall upward trend, but a sudden change occurred in 2017 and 2018. Quarterly runoff follows periodic patterns with multiple characteristic scales, among which the wet and dry periods are evenly distributed. Although the prediction accuracy of long-lasting low flow events has slightly declined, the information features of the time series parts containing these events were all basically captured. The evolution characteristics and permutation analysis jointly reveal that 7d-Runoff logically explained regular variations of runoff based on its self-correlation information of multistage delay. The universal importance of W-level and Sedi-Conc with runoff suggests that the fragile soil structure with degraded vegetation is a main cause of irregular runoff events. The importance of Soil-MC at the San Menxia Station indicates that the sensitivity of the soil environment to runoff is amplified when the natural fluctuations of runoff decrease. This study demonstrates that both the natural environment and human activities have a significant influence on the evolution characteristics of runoff in this basin. The permutation analysis of input variables provides the possibility for interpreting the dynamic response rules of diverse runoff forms predicted by the BC-BiLSTM model.

title: Modelling and Validating the Interrelationships among Barriers to Financial Inclusion of Internal Migrant Labours: An Integrated ISM-MICMAC and SEM Approach
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Modelling and Validating the Interrelationships among Barriers to Financial Inclusion of Internal Migrant Labours: An Integrated ISM-MICMAC and SEM Approach
detail.abstract: The purpose of this study is to identify and investigate the contextual relationships of the key barriers to internal migrant labours' financial inclusion. Using the interpretative structural modeling (ISM) approach, the barriers' contextual relations and hierarchies are formed, and they have been categorized into several categories using MICMAC analysis. Furthermore, the ISM model has been statistically validated using data gathered from a questionnaire-based study of internal migrant labourers using structural equation modelling based on partial least squares (PLS-SEM). The paper creates a structural model by developing relationships and imposing directions among the barriers.

title: What Drives Crypto Prices?
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University and Johns Hopkins University

detail.title: What Drives Crypto Prices?
detail.abstract: We study intraday price discovery in cryptocurrency markets using high-frequency session-level data across global trading zones over March 2024–March 2026. We identify two primary and distinct drivers of crypto price variation. First, the Amihud (2002) illiquidity ratio explains up to 70\% of the magnitude of intraday price movements during the New York morning session (9 AM–12 PM ET), with higher illiquidity systematically associated with larger absolute price changes. This result is robust across most global sessions. However, the illiquidity channel predicts the size of price moves, not their direction. Second, changes in stablecoin prices during the European lunch session (7 AM–9 AM ET) explain up to 90\% of crypto price variation in the subsequent New York morning (9 AM - 12 PM ET) and lunch (12 PM–1 PM ET) sessions. This stablecoin channel is concentrated in price deviations from the dollar peg: using two-stage least squares (2SLS), we show that stablecoin volume carries no predictive power once instrumented, while price deviations retain strong and statistically significant predictive content. Stablecoin-driven predictability dissipates sharply during New York afternoon trading hours, consistent with the influx of informed institutional investors actively rebalancing their portfolios and ETFs. Our findings carry direct implications for financial stability: regulators should focus surveillance on intraday stablecoin price deviations as an early-warning indicator, rather than on volume-based metrics alone. The time-zone asymmetry in predictability further calls for internationally coordinated, session-aware oversight of stablecoin markets.

title: Phase transformation in oxygen pressure leaching of high-lead zinc concentrates for residue reduction and efficiency leaching
affiliations: Honghe University, Honghe University, Honghe University, Kunming University of Science and Technology - Faculty of Metallurgical and Energy Engineering, Kunming University of Science and Technology - Faculty of Metallurgical and Energy Engineering, Kunming University of Science and Technology - Faculty of Metallurgical and Energy Engineering and Kunming University of Science and Technology - Faculty of Metallurgical and Energy Engineering

detail.title: Phase transformation in oxygen pressure leaching of high-lead zinc concentrates for residue reduction and efficiency leaching
detail.abstract: The effective recovery of zinc and other valuable metals from high-Pb zinc sulfide concentrates remains challenging owing to lead jarosite (Pb-J) formation during oxygen pressure leaching. This hazardous waste byproduct hinders metal extraction and significantly increases the yield of leach residues. This study employs a two-stage oxygen pressure leaching process (LHPL) with a "low-temperature reduction followed by high-temperature oxidation" control strategy to selectively regulate iron leaching and suppress Pb-J phase formation. Compared with the two-stage high-pressure high-temperature leaching process (HHPL), the LHPL process increased the leaching efficiencies of zinc, copper, and indium from 96.7%, 65.2%, and 68.9% to 98.6%, 88.3%, and 90.1%, silver enrichment rate improved from 72.0% to 93.1%, and reduce residue yield by 20%, which effectively minimizes residue generation at the source. Mineralogical analysis reveals that the LHPL process stably converts lead into PbSO4 rather than Pb-J. The LHPL residue exhibits a coarser particle size and hydrophobic surface, leading to excellent settling performance and efficient solid–liquid separation, while the process maintains Fe2+ in the first stage to facilitate iron removal and retains soluble Fe3+ in the second stage to accelerate leaching. This approach suppresses Pb-J formation and maximizes iron utilization. These findings provide technical guidance for the reduction of hazardous iron-containing residues.

title: Tariffs across the supply chain
affiliations: European Central Bank (ECB), European Central Bank and Central Bank of Malta

detail.title: Tariffs across the supply chain
detail.abstract: What are the macroeconomic impacts of tariffs on final goods versus intermediate inputs? We set up a two-region, multi-sector model with global production networks, sticky prices and wages, and trade in consumption, investment, and intermediate goods. We show, analytically and quantitatively, that import tariffs on final goods have a smaller negative impact on GDP compared to tariffs on intermediate inputs, as final goods can be more readily substituted domestically. By contrast, tariffs on intermediate inputs lead to larger GDP losses, given the limited substitutability of foreign inputs. Moreover, inflation persistence is lower under tariffs on final goods, whereas tariffs on intermediate goods give rise to persistent cost pressures through production linkages. The results imply that revenue-equivalent import tariffs targeting only final goods can cushion the adverse effects of trade fragmentation.

title: Multi-scale approach to understanding and predicting environmental reactivity in the context of ISR
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Mines Paris - PSL, Mines Paris - PSL, Université Paris-Dauphine, PSL Research University - MINES ParisTech, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Multi-scale approach to understanding and predicting environmental reactivity in the context of ISR
detail.abstract: In situ recovery (ISR) is a worldwide mining technique which accounts for more than 52 % (in 2024) of global U production, thanks to its cost-effectiveness. However, where an ISR process uses sulfuric acid (H2SO4), local underground exploited aquifers’ water quality can be affected by low pH and high concentrations of SO4. Hydrogeochemical processes controlling this groundwater changes are studied here in the context of the planned exploitation of the Zoovch Ovoo deposit in Mongolia, using a multi-scale approach comparing real data with models. At the laboratory scale, experimental data combined with a 1D reactive transport model (RTM) demonstrate that ion-exchange reactions on clay minerals surface are the main geochemical mechanism governing groundwater chemistry (pH and major ions). To consider system heterogeneity and the spatial impact of the ISR process, field data from two pilot cells were combined with a 3D reactive transport model. The model successfully reproduced the field data by considering both ion-exchange and dissolution-precipitation reactions of the mineral phases, especially calcite and gypsum, necessary to explain the water chemistry at larger scale. Vertical and lateral fluid excursions out of the pilot cells were observed depending on the system heterogeneity. This study demonstrated that the relative importance of the various processes investigated depends on the time and distance scales probed. For the short term and U production, heterogeneities and ion-exchange are crucial for explaining the changes in groundwater chemistry. A better understanding and quantification of these processes will help operators optimize production and long-term environmental remediation strategies.

title: Analysis of Billing Mechanisms for Equitable Energy Access in a Distributed Energy System
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Analysis of Billing Mechanisms for Equitable Energy Access in a Distributed Energy System
detail.abstract: The increasing deployment of distributed energy resources (DER) has accelerated the transition toward clean and sustainable energy systems, while raising concerns about equitable energy access among heterogeneous consumers. In distributed energy systems (DES), the distribution of economic benefits is determined by pricing mechanisms such as Net Energy Metering (NEM) and Feed-in Tariff (FiT). While these mechanisms have been extensively studied for renewable energy integration and economic efficiency, their effects on surplus distribution and equity remain underexplored. To address this gap, this paper presents a systematic analytical framework to evaluate the surplus distribution and equity impacts of NEM and FiT in DES. The analysis explicitly links pricing mechanism design to individual consumer net benefits and equitable energy access. It assesses distributional outcomes using a Rawlsian equity criterion that prioritizes improvements for the least-advantaged participants. Case-wise comparative analysis is conducted to identify conditions under which NEM or FiT leads to more equitable outcomes, supported by numerical validation on a standard IEEE PES open dataset. The results highlight inherent trade-offs between efficiency and equity and provide analytical insights to support the design of pricing mechanisms that promote fair, affordable, and sustainable DES.

title: Hydropower Uncertainty in Capacity Expansion: Calibration Against a Hydro-Thermal Scheduling Model
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Canterbury, University of Auckland and University of Canterbury

detail.title: Hydropower Uncertainty in Capacity Expansion: Calibration Against a Hydro-Thermal Scheduling Model
detail.abstract: The global transition to a zero-carbon energy system requires modelling tools that translate decarbonisation targets into actionable investment and operational strategies. Hydropower’s operational flexibility is essential for integrating variable renewables, yet many capacity expansion models (CEMs) rely on deterministic, perfect-foresight assumptions, which can misrepresent system flexibility and produce unrealistic dispatch patterns. We present a model validation framework to evaluate whether a reduced-order hydro uncertainty formulation provides a faithful approximation to stochastic hydro-thermal operational model. GEMSTONE, a two-stage stochastic capacity expansion model with scenario-dependent availability factors and end-of-season storage-gates, is benchmarked against JADE, a high-fidelity SDDP-based hydro-thermal scheduling model, across a range of representative inflow scenarios. Results demonstrate that the storage-gate formulation closely replicates total system operating costs (within [[EQUATION]]) but suppress scenario-specific operational decisions to approximate uncertainty and maintain non-anticipativity. Increasing gate flexibility improves alignment with inflow scenarios but generates perfect-foresight policies. The calibrated reduced-order storage-gate formulation efficiently captures key hydropower uncertainty dynamics. Future work will integrate this approach into high-resolution CEMs with high renewable investments to support large-scale decarbonisation planning. The framework offers energy system modelers a computationally efficient, transferable method for accurately representing hydropower uncertainty in capacity expansion planning studies.

title: Institutional Ownership and Corporate Labor Policies: Evidence from Korean Firms
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Institutional Ownership and Corporate Labor Policies: Evidence from Korean Firms
detail.abstract: This study examines how institutional ownership influences corporate labor policies as part of firms’ resource allocation decisions. As institutional investors including pension funds, private equity funds (PEFs), and other financial institutions have become dominant shareholders in capital markets, their role has expanded beyond monitoring financial performance to shaping broader corporate policies. Using an unbalanced panel dataset of publicly listed non-financial firms in Korea from 2011 to 2024, we employ firm fixed-effects models to analyze the relationship between institutional ownership and labor market outcomes. To address potential endogeneity concerns, we further implement a two-stage least squares (2SLS) approach using industry-level institutional ownership as an instrumental variable. The results indicate that higher institutional ownership is associated with lower employment stability, reflected in reductions in total employment, shorter average employee tenure, and a lower proportion of regular workers. In addition, institutional ownership is negatively related to wage outcomes, including both total wages and average wages per employee, with particularly pronounced effects on core wage components. These findings suggest that institutional investors may influence firms’ labor policies through cost-reduction and efficiency-oriented strategies. We further document substantial heterogeneity across investor types. Public pension funds are associated with relatively stable employment practices, whereas private equity funds and other institutional investors are more strongly linked to workforce reductions and lower wage levels. This heterogeneity highlights the importance of distinguishing among different types of institutional investors when evaluating their real effects on firms. Overall, our findings provide new evidence that institutional ownership affects not only financial outcomes but also real corporate decisions related to labor. This study contributes to the literature on corporate governance and institutional investors by highlighting their broader economic and social implications in emerging markets.

title: Effects of Mismatch between Explicit (eHMI) Cues and Perceived Implicit Cues on Street-crossing Decisions
affiliations: Rice University, Rice University, Rice University and Rice University

detail.title: Effects of Mismatch between Explicit (eHMI) Cues and Perceived Implicit Cues on Street-crossing Decisions
detail.abstract: Previous studies showed that pedestrians rely on both implicit cues (e.g., deceleration) and explicit cues (e.g., eye contact) to decide when to cross the street, and that the effects of mismatches between these cues can influence such decisions which is especially relevant in the era of autonomous vehicle (AV) systems. However, the effect of mismatches between perceived implicit cues and explicit cues on street-crossing decisions, as well as trust, has not been measured. The present study examined how mismatches between the perceived implicit cue of an AV’s deceleration and the explicit cue from the AV’s external human–machine interface (eHMI) affect the percentage of trials in which the participant decided to cross the street, the percentage of trials in which the participant complied with the eHMI cue, response time (RT), and trust in the AV. Participants viewed virtual-reality displays of a vehicle that approached while decelerating, and reported whether they would cross the street. We varied the perceptibility of the deceleration (Can See, Cannot See, Uncertain), initial vehicle speed (20 vs 40 mph), and eHMI cues (Cross, Don’t Cross, No eHMI). When the eHMI cue contradicted the perception of deceleration (e.g., Cross), participants relied primarily on their perception rather than the eHMI cue. Consistency between the eHMI and pedestrians’ perceptions also increased trust; and RTs depended on both the participants’ perceptions and vehicle speed. The effectiveness of an eHMI depends on a pedestrian’s perception of the implicit vehicle’s motion and whether perception is consistent with the eHMI cues.

title: The Digital Distortion in Railway Passenger Well-being: Intrinsic Motivation, Digital Media Usage, and the Moderating Role of On-train Environment
affiliations: University of Tokyo - The University of Tokyo, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Tokyo - The University of Tokyo, Seijo University, University of Tokyo - The University of Tokyo, Toyo University, Toyo University and University of Tokyo - The University of Tokyo

detail.title: The Digital Distortion in Railway Passenger Well-being: Intrinsic Motivation, Digital Media Usage, and the Moderating Role of On-train Environment
detail.abstract: The widespread adoption of information and communication technology (ICT) enables passengers to transform travel into productive time. However, constant internet connectivity creates multitasking environments that do not necessarily improve passengers' subjective well-being (SWB). Based on a survey of railway passengers (N = 461) in the Tokyo metropolitan area, this study elucidated the association between digital media usage and SWB by focusing on interactions among (1) motivation quality, (2) media format, and (3) the on-train environment. Hypothesis testing using cluster analysis and multi-group structural equation modeling (MG-SEM) revealed three key findings. First, intrinsic motivation for selecting activities predicted onboard well-being (OWB) more strongly than the activity content itself. Second, analog media users exhibited the highest OWB, even after controlling for age and physical burden. Conversely, digital media usage revealed a distortion: OWB decreased despite being driven by high intrinsic motivation. Third, the on-train environment exerted a moderating effect. The negative impact of digital usage was significantly more prominent in focus-friendly environments—characterized by abundant travel time and habituation—rather than mere absence of crowding. Furthermore, enhanced OWB significantly spilled over to overall life satisfaction. These findings suggest that internet connectivity in focus-friendly environments excessively consumes cognitive resources, obstructing travel's inherent restorative potential. Consequently, improving passenger well-being requires designing environments as cognitive shelters supporting analog immersion and intentional disconnection, moving beyond merely ensuring connectivity and alleviating congestion.

title: Deposit Insurance Reforms and Bank Risk-Taking: An International Perspective on Discipline and Moral Hazard
affiliations: University of Saskatchewan - Department of Finance and Management Science, University of Saskatchewan and University of Saskatchewan

detail.title: Deposit Insurance Reforms and Bank Risk-Taking: An International Perspective on Discipline and Moral Hazard
detail.abstract: Does expanding deposit insurance coverage to prevent bank runs inadvertently fuel bank risk-taking? Following the Great Financial Crisis, many advanced economies raised deposit insurance limits to protect previously uninsured depositors. We study this trade-off by comparing countries that expanded coverage – the United States, the European Union, and Australia – with Canada and Japan, that kept their deposit insurance schemes unchanged. Using bank-level balance sheet data and bank lending surveys from 2005 to 2019, we show that coverage expansions substantially strengthened deposit funding: banks’ deposit-to-assets ratios rose by 9.32 percentage points and average interest expenses declined. At the same time, banks took more risk. Loan loss reserves (LLR) relative to loans increased by roughly 0.4 percentage points, and credit standards loosened across loan categories, especially in consumer credit, where the net share of banks tightening standards fell by more than 20 percentage points. Interactions with macroeconomic conditions indicate that, after the reforms, both funding structures and LLR became more sensitive to policy rates and financial market volatility, increasing the procyclicality of bank behavior. Overall, our results point to a policy trilemma: expanding deposit insurance coverage stabilizes funding in normal times but weakens depositor discipline and heightens the sensitivity of bank risk-taking to the business and financial cycle.

title: Deposit Insurance and Banking Sector Stability: Evidence from Africa
affiliations: University of St. Andrews, University of Cologne, University of St. Andrews and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Deposit Insurance and Banking Sector Stability: Evidence from Africa
detail.abstract: Using hand-collected data for 54 African countries over 2000 to 2021, this paper provides the first systematic evidence on the relationship between deposit insurance coverage and banking sector stability in Africa. To address endogeneity, we employ the methodology of Calomiris and Chen (2022), exploiting variation in regional and international regulatory pressures as instruments. Contrary to evidence from advanced economies, we find that greater deposit insurance coverage enhances banking sector stability. This stabilising effect operates through two channels: reduced volatility of bank profitability and lower private sector lending, consistent with conservative balance sheet management rather than moral hazard driven risk-taking.

title: Macroeconomic and Sustainability Determinants of BankProfitability: Evidence from U.S. Banks in the Post-CrisisPeriod
affiliations: University of Patras, University of Patras - Business Administration, University of Patras and University of Patras

detail.title: Macroeconomic and Sustainability Determinants of BankProfitability: Evidence from U.S. Banks in the Post-CrisisPeriod
detail.abstract: This study investigates the determinants of U.S. bank profitability in the post-crisisperiod 2010–2021, with a primary focus on the pivotal role of sustainability dynamics.While accounting for traditional bank-specific and macroeconomic controls, our analysisprioritizes the impact of environmental factors on financial performance. The core contribution of this research is twofold. Using panel data from 512 banks, we initially employfixed-effects estimation to establish that renewable energy consumption significantly enhances profitability, whereas energy intensity acts as a detrimental factor. Furthermore,the application of a Panel Smooth Transition Regression (PSTR) framework uncovers evidence of ’selective non-linearity’. We reveal that environmental variables do not merelyinfluence returns linearly but act as regime-shifting catalysts, the transmission of internal bank characteristics to profitability is fundamentally contingent upon the economy’ssustainability regime. These findings suggest that environmental transitions have superseded traditional market structures in inducing structural breaks in bank performance,offering critical insights for policymakers and managers navigating an increasingly carbonconscious financial landscape

title: From Wires to Welfare: Evidence on Digital Infrastructure and Job Quality from Broadband China
affiliations: Chongqing Technology and Business University, Chongqing Technology and Business University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: From Wires to Welfare: Evidence on Digital Infrastructure and Job Quality from Broadband China
detail.abstract: The pivotal role of digital infrastructure in advancing the digital economy is widely recognized, yet its implications for job quality remain underexplored. This study develops a theoretical framework linking digital infrastructure to job quality and empirically tests it using the Broadband China strategy as an exogenous shock. Drawing on CHFS data from 2011-2021, we employ a multi-period difference-in-differences model with instrumental variable estimation and robustness checks. Results show that digital infrastructure significantly enhances job quality through four channels: strengthening regional innovation, stimulating entrepreneurship, improving total factor productivity, and promoting industrial upgrading. Benefits are greater for individuals with agricultural hukou, lower education levels, and low-prestige occupations, highlighting its inclusive impact. These findings provide micro-level evidence of the welfare-enhancing effects of digital infrastructure, offering policy implications for promoting high-quality, full employment and narrowing the digital divide. Overall, digital infrastructure development is an effective means to improve job quality.

title: Do Asset Prices Help Predict Inflation? Evidence from Individual Stock Prices
affiliations: Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE) - School of Economics, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE) - School of Economics and Peking University

detail.title: Do Asset Prices Help Predict Inflation? Evidence from Individual Stock Prices
detail.abstract: This paper revisits the predictive power of asset prices for inflation, focusing on individual stock prices rather than aggregate indices. Using a large panel data of firm-level stock prices and applying machine learning techniques, we demonstrate that individual stock prices significantly enhance the accuracy of inflation forecasts, particularly over medium-to long-term horizons and during periods of high inflationary and deflationary pressure. Compared to composite and industry-level stock indices, other aggregate asset prices, and Fama-French factors, individual stock prices contain valuable heterogeneous information, offering richer insights for inflation forecasting. These findings provide new empirical support for macro-finance theory, affirming the predictive value of asset prices from a micro-level perspective.

title: Dollar-Cost Averaging and Self-Annuitization under Geometric Brownian Motion: Moments and Symmetry
affiliations: Hong Kong US invest

detail.title: Dollar-Cost Averaging and Self-Annuitization under Geometric Brownian Motion: Moments and Symmetry
detail.abstract: For investors receiving a windfall, lump-sum investing dominates dollar-cost averaging (DCA) in expected value; any DCA plan should thus be limited to months, not decades. It is best viewed as a behavioral tool to overcome inertia, not as a strategy for wealth maximization. Retirees face a similar but more consequential decision spanning three to four decades. Dynastic wealth maximizers (à la Barro) should self-annuitize to harvest the equity premium, as accepting the risk-free rate foregoes substantial wealth. In contrast, retirees facing longevity risk (à la Yaari) confront a genuine trade-off: self-annuitization offers higher expected consumption when interest rates are low, but only a commercial annuity provides true longevity insurance. After framing these practical use cases, the paper derives closed-form expressions for the first two moments of terminal wealth under continuous dollar-cost averaging and selfannuitization within a geometric Brownian motion framework. The analysis reveals a clear mathematical symmetry between accumulation and decumulation, but with different practical implications due to differences in horizon and investor objectives.

title: Optimal Rule-Based General A+B Design in Phase I Clinical Trials
affiliations: Washington University in St. Louis - School of Medicine and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Optimal Rule-Based General A+B Design in Phase I Clinical Trials
detail.abstract: Background: Lin et al. studied the statistical properties of rule-based general A+B designs using true toxicity probabilities, without and with dose de-escalation, and derived exact formulae for key statistical quantities essential for phase I clinical trials. Methods: We systematically evaluate the impact of the parameters of A, B, C, D and E on the key statistical quantities across five dose levels within the A+B=6 framework. Simulation studies are conducted with true toxicity probabilities generated using a dose-toxicity model on known prior toxicity probabilities. Results: General A+B designs with dose de-escalation are more conservative than those without dose de-escalation. For either presence or absence of dose de-escalation, 1) under an under-toxic environment, the 33222 design is the best design and 24113 design is the second one, but 33222 design requires two more patients expected to be treated than 24113 design. 2) under a moderate-toxic and over-toxic environment, 24113 and 42111 design demonstrates an absolute and evident superiority, respectively. 3) under an unknown-toxic environment, 33122 design is the optimal choice but requires a larger total number of patients expected to be treated. 4) under an over-/unknown-toxic environment, the traditional “3+3” is one of the top two smallest total number of patients expected to be treated and patients experiencing a dose-limiting toxicity. Conclusions: Some general designs have superior performance than traditional “3+3” design, having the target toxicity level closest to target toxicity rate (TTR) and higher number of patients treated at the dose levels with toxicity probabilities close to TTR.

title: Transition finance and corporate default risk: Evidence from China's Green Finance Pilot Zones
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Transition finance and corporate default risk: Evidence from China's Green Finance Pilot Zones
detail.abstract: This paper studies whether transition-finance policy affects firm-level default risk. We examine China's 2017 Green Finance Reform and Innovation Pilot Zones (GFPZs) and estimate two-way fixed-effects difference-in-differences models on 746 A-share firms from 2007 to 2021 (6,304 firm-year observations). The main outcome is market-implied default risk measured as Risk (= -DD_KMV). The baseline estimate is negative (-0.2537; province-clustered SE = 0.2416; 95% CI: [-0.7273, 0.2198]). Event-study estimates with binned pre-treatment leads show no systematic pre-trend and mostly negative post-policy coefficients. Given only five treated provinces, we report few-cluster diagnostics transparently (wild-cluster bootstrap p = 0.5238; randomization-inference p = 0.4067; placebo assignment p-values 0.1700 one-sided and 0.3900 two-sided), and placebo-in-time tests in the pre-policy period show no effect. Mechanism evidence indicates de-risking in firm financing (lower short-term borrowings and lower total borrowings) and higher green innovation, while ESG scores respond weakly. Overall, the evidence supports a negative association between GFPZ exposure and market-implied default risk, with conservative inference indicating substantial uncertainty around average effects.

title: Boom-Bust Interdependence and Contagion in Emerging Equity Markets
affiliations: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV) (Formerly University of Texas-Pan American) and Texas A&M University (TAMU) - San Antonio

detail.title: Boom-Bust Interdependence and Contagion in Emerging Equity Markets
detail.abstract: We examine how boom-bust regimes emerge and propagate across major emerging equity markets. Using the generalized supremum augmented Dickey-Fuller (GSADF) framework of Phillips et al. (2015), we date-stamp multiple episodes of explosive (bubble) and implosive (crash) behavior in twelve emerging stock indices and the U.S. S&P 500 over 1999 - 2023. We then estimate state‑timing logistic regressions that map bubble and crash states in source markets to the probability that target markets are in each state, allowing us to distinguish three channels: interdependence (simultaneous same‑state co‑occurrence), contagion (lagged same‑state propagation), and asset rotation (lagged opposite‑state links). As a continuous benchmark, we implement a Dynamic Conditional Correlation DCC-GARCH model to trace time‑varying return correlations and relate correlation spikes to the breadth of exuberant regimes. We document frequent and heterogeneous bubble and crash regimes, with markets such as Indonesia, India, and Chile spending roughly one‑fifth to one‑quarter of the sample in bubbles and experiencing recurrent crashes, while Malaysia, South Korea, and Taiwan exhibit shorter and less frequent exuberant phases. Logistic estimates reveal strong interdependence: the states of a small set of hubs, Brazil, Malaysia, Mexico, South Korea, and the United States, are highly informative about the simultaneous states of other markets. We also find economically meaningful contagion, especially in bubbles, and pockets of asset rotation, where bubbles in some markets signal crashes in others and vice versa. DCC correlations surge when many markets are jointly exuberant but are largely silent about sequencing and direction. Our joint GSADF-logit-DCC framework therefore complements standard correlation-based analyses and yields compact, regime‑aware diagnostics for investors and policymakers concerned with emerging market boom-bust risk.

title: Risk-coupled optimization of offshore drilling parameters with multi-source data fusion and dual-pathway Pareto convergence
affiliations: Yangtze University, Yangtze University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Yangtze University, Yangtze University, Yangtze University, Yangtze University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Risk-coupled optimization of offshore drilling parameters with multi-source data fusion and dual-pathway Pareto convergence
detail.abstract: Offshore drilling operations face harsh metocean conditions, complex wellbore configurations, and extremely high day rates, where any downhole incident can cause severe economic losses and hazards. Optimizing drilling parameters to maximize the rate of penetration (ROP) and minimize mechanical specific energy (MSE) while ensuring downhole safety is therefore essential. However, this dual objective is inherently conflicting and further complicated by downhole risks that surface data alone cannot characterize. This paper proposes a risk-coupled dual-objective optimization framework that integrates near-bit subsea memory data with surface mud-logging data through a multi-source heterogeneous-frequency data fusion pipeline, incorporating bit wear coefficient (DRIMP), stick-slip index (SSI), and lateral and axial vibration RMS as unified safety constraints alongside conventional equipment limits. A Sort-Filter-Skyline algorithm extracts the Pareto non-dominated front, from which two complementary convergence pathways—entropy-weighted TOPSIS for objective global evaluation and tolerant stratified sequencing for engineering-target-oriented decision—yield executable WOB–RPM combinations. Field application demonstrates that the TOPSIS pathway achieves a 9.66% ROP gain and 35.48% MSE reduction with all risk indicators improved, while the stratified sequencing pathway achieves an 18.65% ROP gain and 5.89% MSE reduction with all safety indicators within acceptable limits. The framework provides field engineers with mutually validating decision references balancing efficiency and safety.

title: Tokenization, Transparency, and Time on Market: Empirical evidence from a Blockchain-Based Real Estate Market
affiliations: University of Regensburg - International Real Estate Business School (IREBS), LMU Munich School of Management and University of Regensburg - International Real Estate Business School (IREBS)

detail.title: Tokenization, Transparency, and Time on Market: Empirical evidence from a Blockchain-Based Real Estate Market
detail.abstract: Tokenized real-estate markets, in which fractionalized digital claims on individual properties are traded, create an unusually transparent setting in which listing histories, price revisions, and execution outcomes are publicly traceable. This paper applies standard Time on Market (ToM) frameworks to tokenized real estate for the first time and studies listing behavior, seller adjustment, and marketing time for individual real-estate tokens. Using complete listing and transaction data from a large blockchain-based peer-to-peer marketplace, we compile a unique dataset covering more than 111,000 listings and more than 72,000 sales for 731 tokenized rental residential properties in the United States and Latin America from 2020 to 2025. Using OLS and accelerated failure time models, we find that overpricing relative to the redemption benchmark strongly prolongs ToM, while each additional percentage point of downward revision shortens remaining ToM by approximately 6%, conditional on the premium that remains after the revision. Holding total price concessions constant, listings sold after a single decisive price reduction achieve higher final premia than otherwise similar listings repriced gradually, consistent with repeated observable reductions signaling a declining reservation price and inviting buyer delay. Overall, the study shows that tokenization makes liquidity and execution outcomes more tightly linked to transparent relative pricing and publicly observable seller adjustment, with implications for increasingly transparent digital listing platforms in real-estate markets more broadly.

title: Integration of stochastic methods at multiple time scales for drought risk estimation through long term simulation
affiliations: Alma Mater Studiorum University of Bologna and Alma Mater Studiorum University of Bologna

detail.title: Integration of stochastic methods at multiple time scales for drought risk estimation through long term simulation
detail.abstract: Droughts are among the most severe and impactful environmental disasters affecting humanity. A key step towards fostering a proactive approach in drought risk management and thus mitigating the impacts of drought events, suggests a deeper understanding of the statistics of the natural processes giving rise to such hazards. In this context, the detailed study of precipitation statistics and the underlying surprise factor associated with their low frequency behaviours, using appropriate stochastic simulation methods, are crucial for drought risk estimation and forecasting of extended rainfall deficits. In this work, we focus on the estimation of frequency, duration and severity of multi-year droughts, which are recognised as a key risk for water resources management and supply. We propose a novel approach based on the integration of the CoSMoS stochastic model, which simulates intermittency, variability and interdependence, characterizing precipitation records at daily time scale, with an ARFIMA (0,d,0) model to capture the long-term persistence at annual time scale. The proposed integrated stochastic approach is tested using the precipitation time series of Bologna, one of the longest daily rainfall time series available worldwide. Following a Monte Carlo simulation approach, 500 synthetic 100-year long precipitation time series are generated, using the integrated stochastic model, and are further analysed and compared by applying run theory to estimate multi-year drought risk through the probabilistic evaluation of drought frequency, duration, intensity and maximum deficit across the Bologna region. The results show that the integrated CoSMoS+ARFIMA model outperforms state-of-the-art prediction methods, therefore offering an innovative support to the management of drought risk.

title: Forecasting Bitcoin realized volatility under regime switching and delayed mean reversion
affiliations: Beijing Normal University, Beijing Normal University and Beijing Normal University

detail.title: Forecasting Bitcoin realized volatility under regime switching and delayed mean reversion
detail.abstract: Accurate volatility forecasting is important for risk management, portfolio decisions, and derivative valuation in cryptocurrency markets. This paper proposes a regime-switching continuous-time model for Bitcoin realized volatility that combines a standard Ornstein--Uhlenbeck (OU) process with a distributed-delay OU process. The framework is intended to capture both latent changes in market conditions and persistent dependence in volatility dynamics. Model estimation is implemented through an Expectation--Maximization procedure under latent state switching, and forecasts are obtained by combining regime-specific conditional dynamics with filtered state probabilities. Using daily log-realized variance constructed from high-frequency Bitcoin prices, we show that the proposed model provides a better in-sample fit than single-regime OU and delay-OU benchmarks and identifies economically interpretable latent regimes. The estimated state sequence indicates that Bitcoin volatility is mainly characterized by a persistent low-volatility regime together with a limited number of high-volatility stress episodes. Out-of-sample evidence for 2025 further shows that the proposed specification outperforms OU, delay-OU, AR(1), AR(3), and HAR models in volatility forecasting. The results suggest that jointly accounting for delayed mean reversion and regime heterogeneity improves Bitcoin volatility forecasting and offers useful insights into the dynamics of stress in cryptocurrency markets.

title: Sensing Culture, Seizing Markets: The Contingent Role of Foreign Market Turbulence in Driving SME International Performance
affiliations: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana, Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana, Kumasi Technical University, Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana, Akenten Appiah-Menka University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development (AAMUSTED) - Akenten Appiah-Menka University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development, Kumasi Technical University, Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana and Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana

detail.title: Sensing Culture, Seizing Markets: The Contingent Role of Foreign Market Turbulence in Driving SME International Performance
detail.abstract: Despite widespread recognition of culture's strategic importance in international operations, cultural intelligence research remains predominantly individual-centric, leaving organizational-level theorizing underdeveloped. Integrating dynamic capabilities theory with the attention-based view, we reconceptualize cultural intelligence as an organizational meta-attention capability that facilitates adaptive reconfiguration in culturally complex markets. Analyzing multi-wave data from 208 internationalizing Ghanaian SMEs, we find that organizational cultural intelligence enhances international performance both directly and indirectly through foreign market adaptability. While the index of moderated mediation was nonsignificant, conditional indirect effects reveal that the mediation pathway strengthens significantly under high foreign market turbulence. This study advances cultural intelligence scholarship by empirically validating firm-level conceptualization, explicating adaptive mediation mechanisms, and identifying environmental boundary conditions that shape the capability-performance link.

title: When Compassionate AI Becomes a Leader: The Role of Emotional Transportation in Human–AI Collaboration
affiliations: Central South University, Central South University and Zhongnan University of Economics and Law

detail.title: When Compassionate AI Becomes a Leader: The Role of Emotional Transportation in Human–AI Collaboration
detail.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI)—particularly agentic AI—becomes increasingly embedded in organizational collaboration, AI systems are beginning to assume roles that involve guiding, coordinating, and supporting human work. Yet, employees often resist the leadership role of AI agents. A key reason is that AI is assumed as mechanistic and lacking compassion, a quality central to human-centered organizing and employee well-being. Drawing on emotional transportation theory, this research examines how compassionate AI capacities enable the emergence of AI leadership in collaborative work settings. We conceptualize compassionate AI capacities as AI agents’ ability to recognize employees’ emotional needs and respond with intentional, supportive actions. We theorize that when AI agents exhibit such capacities, they can trigger emotional transportation, whereby employees become psychologically immersed in emotionally meaningful interactions and come to perceive the AI agent as socially expressive, caring, and purposefully supportive. This increases employees’ willingness to accept guidance from AI, thereby enabling the emergence of AI leadership. We further identify perceived artificiality as a key boundary condition shaping when compassionate AI capacities translate into leadership emergence. Results of two independent studies, i.e., a field survey (Study 1) and a scenario-based experiment (Study 2), provided empirical support for the proposed model. This research contributes to the information systems literature by elucidating the socio-emotional mechanisms through which compassionate, agentic AI shapes human behavioral responses, offering insights for the design and evaluation of compassionate AI systems in organizational contexts.

title: Behavior Is Not Leadership: The Prevalence of Formal Fallacy Endorsement in Leadership Judgements
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Luxembourg School of Business and Zagreb School of Economics and Management

detail.title: Behavior Is Not Leadership: The Prevalence of Formal Fallacy Endorsement in Leadership Judgements
detail.abstract: Certain scholarly research and popular discourse both take for granted that behavioral-based conceptions of leadership are sufficient to justify the conferring of leadership status. This article critically examines the epistemic foundations of such assumptions by empirically investigating the prevalence of a specific logical error, the fallacy of the undistributed middle, in common leadership judgments. Drawing on survey data from 233 managerial and non-managerial participants across industries, the study compares responses to simplified behavioral leadership claims and to structurally explicit formulations that reveal their underlying inferential form. Across a range of behaviors prominently promoted in contemporary leadership discourse, respondents consistently endorsed logically invalid conclusions, indicating that leadership judgments often rest on unexamined and flawed reasoning. Managers were significantly more likely than non-managers to commit the fallacy. The article contributes to critical leadership studies by exposing a systematic pattern of fallacious reasoning underlying widely accepted leadership claims and by highlighting the implications of such epistemic weaknesses for leadership research, education, and practice.

title: From Diversity to Decarbonization: Gender-Diverse Boards as Catalysts of Climate Leadership and Innovation
affiliations: University of Southampton, Politecnico di Bari and University of Portsmouth

detail.title: From Diversity to Decarbonization: Gender-Diverse Boards as Catalysts of Climate Leadership and Innovation
detail.abstract: This study develops and tests a sociocognitive leadership and governance explanation of how gender diversity within corporate boards catalyzes innovation in climate change mitigation. Building on social identity theory and extending insights from upper echelon theory and contemporary leadership research, we argue that gender-diverse boards function as collective leadership systems that enhance organizations’ capacity to interpret and respond to environmental challenges. Specifically, gender diversity is proposed to generate cognitive variety, ethical reflexivity, and stakeholder-oriented reasoning within board deliberations - mechanisms that strengthen strategic leadership for sustainability-oriented innovation. When these dynamics reach a sufficient threshold of representation, they are expected to translate into governance innovations capable of materially reducing corporate carbon emissions. To empirically evaluate this framework, the study analyses a panel of 235 FTSE 350 firms between 2019 and 2023 using random-effects regression techniques. The results reveal a significant negative association between board gender diversity and firms’ verified carbon emissions, demonstrating that inclusive leadership structures foster measurable environmental innovation and adaptive strategic decision-making. Interestingly, neither female directors’ educational attainment nor industry carbon intensity significantly moderates this relationship, indicating that the mechanisms underlying environmental performance are rooted primarily in internal leadership processes and identity-driven collaboration rather than formal credentials or sectoral context. By linking board composition to objective emissions outcomes rather than disclosure proxies, this study contributes to research on corporate governance, strategic leadership, and sustainability. It reconceptualizes gender diversity as a sociocognitive leadership capability: a collective resource that enhances organizations’ ability to navigate the institutional and strategic complexities of decarbonization.

title: Contribution as the Telos of Ambition: An Integrative Conceptual Model of Fulfillment in High Performers
affiliations: Independent researcher

detail.title: Contribution as the Telos of Ambition: An Integrative Conceptual Model of Fulfillment in High Performers
detail.abstract: A high-performance culture frequently presents wealth, status, and personal success as the highest ends of ambition. However, across philosophical, religious, and cultural traditions, human flourishing has been framed not as individual accumulation but as contribution to communal life. Modern psychology and sociology echo these insights, and neuroscientific evidence further shows that prosocial behaviors activate biological reward pathways, suggesting that contribution is biologically encoded as fulfilling rather than a mere cultural ideal. Despite this convergence, no integrative model links these insights. This study fills this gap by introducing the contribution-as-telos model, which reframes ambition along three interrelated dimensions: telos, redirecting goals from accumulation to generativity; identity, shifting achievement from compensatory proof to integrated agency; and participation, expanding concern from self-interest to stewardship within interconnected systems. For high performers, this model highlights the opportunity to cultivate sustainable impact through contribution, thus overcoming the risk of exceptional achievement paired with existential non-fulfillment when ambition is self-focused. Theoretically, it lays a foundation for operationalizing “contribution orientation” as a measurable construct, informing leadership frameworks, organizational practice, and longitudinal research on fulfillment beyond extrinsic success. Practically, it suggests narrative and interpretive strategies that reframe goals, identities, and legacies around stewardship, generativity, and enduring communal impact.

title: Gratitude as a Mediator of the Role of Prophetic Leadership on Employee Well-Being
affiliations: Universitas Islam Indonesia and Universitas Islam Indonesia

detail.title: Gratitude as a Mediator of the Role of Prophetic Leadership on Employee Well-Being
detail.abstract: This study aims to examine the role of gratitude as a mediator of prophetic leadership on employee well-being. The major hypothesis of this study is that gratitude will mediate the role of prophetic leadership on employee well-being. The minor hypotheses of this study are that prophetic leadership will play a positive role on employee well-being, prophetic leadership will play a positive role on employee gratitude, and gratitude will play a positive role on employee well-being. Participants in this study consisted of 72 respondents (40 females, 32 males) of a food and beverage (F&B) company in Magelang. The measurement instruments used included the Prophetic Leadership Scale (PLS), the Islamic Gratitude Scale (IGS-10), and the Employee Well-Being Scale (EWBS). The results of the mediation analysis showed that gratitude was proven to be a full mediator of the role of prophetic leadership on employee well-being, indicated by a significant indirect role (estimate = 0.1532; Z = 3.66; p < 0.001). Employees who perceive their leaders as embodying prophetic values ​​such as sidik, amanah, tabligh, and fatanah experience higher levels of gratitude, which ultimately improves their well-being. This finding has important practical implications: organizations in the F&B sector can improve employee well-being by strengthening prophetic leadership practices and developing gratitude as a psychological resource in the workplace.

title: Quantitative research on the relationship between leadership and employee voice – a comprehensive overview of the operationalization and methods
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Quantitative research on the relationship between leadership and employee voice – a comprehensive overview of the operationalization and methods
detail.abstract: Employee voice has been the focus of research particularly within the domain of management. In recent years, numerous conceptual reviews have taken stock, integrated diverse disciplines, and shaped future research perspectives. Thereby, leadership has been identified as a pivotal variable to affect employees' propensity to voice and withhold their thoughts and concerns. Although much is known about this relationship from a theoretical perspective, the empirical evidence concerning it does not allow for a straightforward evaluation due to inconsistent measurements and analyses lacking causal inferences. We systematically review 161 empirical studies on the relationship between leadership and employee voice and silence, focusing on the operationalization and methods. Based on our findings, we derive suggestions on how to improve scientific rigor with respect to operationalizations and methods in this field.

title: A Rapid Decision-Making Framework for Piling Schemes in Levee Breach Scenarios: Integrating Physical Constraints with Deep Learning
affiliations: Northeastern University, Northeastern University, Southeast University, Northeastern University (USA), Northeastern University, Northeastern University, Northeastern University, Northeastern University and Southeast University

detail.title: A Rapid Decision-Making Framework for Piling Schemes in Levee Breach Scenarios: Integrating Physical Constraints with Deep Learning
detail.abstract: Traditional levee breach closure methods rely on material filling or vessel sinking, which poses challenges of low efficiency and insufficient safety. The combination of pile sinking with closuring materials can rapidly construct a stable closure structure, which serves as a critical emergency response technology to prevent breach expansion. As piles act as the primary load-bearing structure against hydrodynamic forces, the pile sinking scheme directly affects closure efficiency and safety. Therefore, it is essential to rapidly establish the pile sinking scheme based on real-time hydrodynamic conditions. To this end, the paper proposes an intelligent decision-making method for pile sinking schemes that integrates physical constraints with deep learning. A low-cost hydrodynamic simulation of breach-pile interaction, validated against field measurements at a 66×86 grid resolution, was conducted to establish a reliable dataset of cross-sectional flow velocity and water depth. Based on the small data set, a physics constrained conditional generative adversarial network is developed to generate training samples that strictly adhere to physical laws, thereby effectively overcoming the challenge of data scarcity. A pile sinking prediction network with embedded soft physical constraints is designed to ensure the predicted schemes are both data driven and mechanically reasonable. The results demonstrate that the generative adversarial network achieves a Jensen–Shannon divergence of only 0.000652 between the generated and true distributions, which is outperform the variational autoencoder. The prediction network attains an R² above 0.98 for key pile scheme parameters of pile spacing, depth of inserting the soil and pile row. The study provides an intelligent decision-making framework for rapid pile sinking scheme selection in levee breaches, which effectively integrates data driven learning with physical laws.

title: A Matheuristic Method for a Time-Dependent Heterogeneous Vehicle Routing Problem with Delivery Options
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, National University of Singapore (NUS), affiliation not provided to SSRN, Hasselt University and National University of Singapore (NUS)

detail.title: A Matheuristic Method for a Time-Dependent Heterogeneous Vehicle Routing Problem with Delivery Options
detail.abstract: Autonomous Delivery Vehicles (ADV) and Shared Delivery Locations (SDL) offer potential to reduce labor costs and congestion, and improve sustainability in urban last-mile logistics. Yet their effectiveness depends on customer acceptance, as customers may reject ADV- or SDL-based services due to convenience, availability, or technology-trust concerns. To capture these realities, we formulate the Time-Dependent Heterogeneous Vehicle Routing Problem with Delivery Options (TD-HVRPDO), which jointly models autonomous and manned fleets, home and SDL delivery modes, customer-specific acceptance constraints, and time-dependent travel times under urban congestion. The model captures the operational synergy between ADV and SDL: SDL consolidates demand and relaxes time-window constraints, while ADV enables labor-free servicing of aggregated delivery points. We develop a hybrid matheuristic integrating Column Generation, Large Neighborhood Search, and Route-based Search. Computational experiments show that our approach produces high-quality solutions more efficiently than a commercial solver and benchmark methods. The numerical results show that joint ADV–SDL deployment reduces emission-relevant operational burdens such as detours, repeated access trips, and low vehicle utilization, particularly under congested conditions.

title: SUPERMARKETS AND THE POLITICS OF PROFITABILITY: THE ROLES OF MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTING IN FRAMING CONTESTS IN PUBLIC INQUIRIES
affiliations: University of Sydney Business School, The University of Sydney and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: SUPERMARKETS AND THE POLITICS OF PROFITABILITY: THE ROLES OF MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTING IN FRAMING CONTESTS IN PUBLIC INQUIRIES
detail.abstract: Amid escalating cost-of-living pressures, supermarket pricing has become a flashpoint for public and political scrutiny across much of the Western world. This paper examines how management accounting was mobilized within the 2024 Australian Senate Select Committee on Supermarket Prices, an inquiry into pricing practices, profitability, and market power. Drawing on a rich corpus of written submissions and public-hearing testimony, we analyze how representatives from Australia’s two largest supermarkets, Coles and Woolworths, deployed internal accounting metrics, visual artifacts, and calculative explanations to shape framing contests over grocery inflation and profit levels. Building on framing research, we identify three analytically distinct roles of management accounting in public framing contests: anchoring, selectively presenting accounting metrics to lend evidentiary support to performance interpretations; relativising, directing attention to other parties and contextual elements (competitors, suppliers, economic conditions) to support positions; and enacting, showcasing accounting tools and gestures to perform responsiveness to concerns. Taken together, these roles illuminate how management accounting operates as a constitutive force in public inquiries, shaping both what counts as credible evidence and how responsibility is publicly allocated in contested arenas.

title: A Stochastic Two Stage Mixed Integer Programming Approach to Vertiport Network Design Under Adoption Uncertainty
affiliations: University of South Florida and University of South Florida

detail.title: A Stochastic Two Stage Mixed Integer Programming Approach to Vertiport Network Design Under Adoption Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Urban Air Mobility (UAM) promises fast and on demand transport through electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft; however, its success depends heavily on vertiport network design under uncertain future demand. This study develops a two-stage stochastic mixed-integer programming model for vertiport location and passenger demand estimation that incorporates the heterogeneity of traveler adoption. Five adoption classes are defined using Rogers’ diffusion of innovations framework (Innovators, Early Adopters, Early Majority, Late Majority, and Laggards), with their population shares used as scenario probabilities in the stochastic model. In each scenario, travelers are assumed to adopt UAM according to that group’s switching threshold when comparing UAM with ground generalized cost. The analysis uses tour-based round trips on disaggregate travel data to ensure consistent access and egress ground modes and to provide a more realistic representation of UAM demand. A case study in Tampa Bay Region validated the methodology and revealed significant insights for policymaking and operations. The results show that innovators and early adopters generate most UAM demand and revenue, while later adopters contribute relatively little even in dense networks. Sensitivity analysis highlight that expanding the number of vertiports steadily increases demand, but after 60–70 vertiports this growth slows down. Compared with the deterministic benchmark network, the stochastic design provides broader geographic coverage, extending benefits to suburban and exurban counties while maintaining core urban hubs. This framework, by incorporating adoption uncertainty into a tour-based stochastic optimization, provides a valuable tool to anticipate future demand and to design networks with broader coverage and stronger robustness to adoption heterogeneity, from early market entry to late UAM adoption.

title: Low-altitude network design in urban area with navigational conflict
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, The University of Hong Kong - University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) - Department of Civil Engineering and Huazhong University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Low-altitude network design in urban area with navigational conflict
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the low-altitude network design problem with given origin-destination (OD) urban logistics delivery demand to avoid conflict among flight routes. Each flight route is experiences taking-off, flat-flying, and landing stages. Different companies with different OD pairs pursuing low flight cost would cause the conflict among fight routes. In this paper, we consider the height allocation problem among multiple OD pairs to avoid conflict among flight routes in the sense of minimization of the total system cost. The problem can be captured by a 0-1 integer programming model by discretizing the continuous low-altitude height. The visibility graph method and the Dijkstra shortest path algorithm are adopted to solve the three-dimensional obstacle-routing problem with the consideration of the airspace restriction, urban buildings and flight safety for a given flight height and OD pair. The flight conflict can be simplified to the height allocation among different OD pairs. A real-world megacity of middle China with over 0.12 billion buildings is adopted to illustrate the proposed model and algorithm.

title: Economic elasticity and resilience in microgrids with V2G, flexible deferrable demand, and varying renewable penetration levels
affiliations: Yarmouk University

detail.title: Economic elasticity and resilience in microgrids with V2G, flexible deferrable demand, and varying renewable penetration levels
detail.abstract: This paper studies the trade-off between economic efficiency and operational reliability in a grid-connected microgrid (MG) under varying renewable energy penetration levels. A day-ahead scheduling model is developed over a 24-hour horizon using DC optimal power flow.
