The goal is to minimize total operating cost while considering generation, energy exchange with the utility grid, energy storage operation, and flexible demand scheduling. The MG includes conventional dispatchable units, renewable energy resources, energy storage systems (ESSs) including electric vehicles, and deferrable loads (DLs). The MG is interconnected with the external grid, and the model incorporates key operational constraints, including generator ramping limits, storage state-of-charge dynamics, time-dependent energy requirements of DLs, nodal active power balance, and transmission line capacity limits. Locational marginal prices (LMPs) are used to provide economic signals for optimal operation and energy trading. To enhance understanding system behavior under changing renewable conditions, the concept of economic elasticity is presented to measure cost sensitivity to renewable penetration level, while structural resilience is used to evaluate performance under grid total and partial contingencies. Particular attention is paid to the contribution of DLs and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) flexibility as a means for supply-demand matching. The simulation results for a six-bus MG system confirm that increased renewable penetration can lead to a substantial reduction in operating costs, even achieving economic savings under favorable conditions. Furthermore, coordinated scheduling of flexible loads and V2G resources improves the overall MG resilience and reduces baseline costs by up to 72%, thus highlighting the importance of flexibility-based MG operation.

title: Curved Greeks: A Geometric Layer for Option P&L Adjustments
affiliations: , Complutense University of Madrid and Comillas Pontifical University - Department of Quantitative Methods

detail.title: Curved Greeks: A Geometric Layer for Option P&L Adjustments
detail.abstract: We develop a modular, coordinate-invariant geometric layer for the short-horizon quadratic P&L approximations used in option hedging. The usual Taylor Hessian is chart-dependent, so second-order P&L can change under reparameterization (spot, forward and log-forward). We replace it with a covariant Hessian associated with an affine connection, making the quadratic term an intrinsic scalar. Desk adjustments enter through two local quadratic inputs: a target curvature form, used to calibrate a market-implied connection (e.g., Vanna-Volga or, when available, local fits to realized P&L) while preserving first-order hedge Greeks; and a quadratic trade-cost model whose pullback under a rebalancing policy defines a Riemannian metric on the state. The metric's Levi-Civita connection yields liquidity-adjusted curved Greeks and geodesic (locally least-cost) hedge schedules. Applying costs to net hedge trades makes portfolio netting effects explicit. Calibrations reduce to small linear systems with clear spanning/conditioning requirements. Two illustrative FX barrier case studies (EURUSD and USDTRY) demonstrate regimes where smile curvature is negligible and where liquidity dominates. The framework is local and model-agnostic, and extends by adding further quadratic penalties (risk normalization, scenarios, capital/xVA).

title: Network, Norms, and Trust: Configurational Analysis of Social Capital in Local Governments
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Gachon University

detail.title: Network, Norms, and Trust: Configurational Analysis of Social Capital in Local Governments
detail.abstract: This study reconceptualizes social capital as a collective-level structural resource manageable by local governments and empirically diagnoses regional variations through fuzzy-set mapping analysis. Adopting the Local Social Capital (LSC) framework (Seo et al., 2024), we distinguish three core dimensions—network, norms, and trust—measured through quantitative indicators at the collective level. Analyzing 28 basic-level local governments in Gyeonggi Province using fuzzy-set calibration and multi-dimensional mapping, we find that local government social capital exhibits distinct configurational types rather than distributing along a single continuum. Only a limited number of municipalities achieve high-level integrated social capital where all three dimensions are simultaneously developed, while the majority show partial imbalances or comprehensive vulnerabilities. Two-dimensional mapping demonstrates that trust-norm, network-trust, and network-norm combinations produce qualitatively different structures, and three-dimensional spatial mapping further categorizes local governments into four types: high-level integrated, partially balanced, biased/single-strength, and low-level vulnerable LSC. Theoretically, the study operationalizes Arendt's (1958) public-private distinction to delimit policy-relevant social capital; methodologically, it demonstrates fuzzy-set techniques as effective tools for capturing configurational complexity. Policy implications emphasize differentiated strategies tailored to each locality's configurational position, providing empirical validation of the LSC framework and practical guidance for managing social capital as a strategic resource for sustainable development.

title: Policy Reforms for Asset-Backed Securities in the Era of Climate Change

detail.title: Policy Reforms for Asset-Backed Securities in the Era of Climate Change
detail.abstract: Climate change has emerged as a systemic risk to global financial systems, with asset-backed securities increasingly exposed to physical and transition-related climate threats. This study examines how existing regulatory and policy frameworks governing asset-backed securities fall short in addressing climate-induced risks and explores reform pathways that can enhance resilience and financial stability. Using a qualitative synthesis of contemporary academic literature and policy-oriented research, the study identifies key vulnerabilities in securitization markets, including inadequate climate risk disclosure, mispricing of long-term environmental risks, and regulatory fragmentation. The findings indicate that policy reforms integrating climate risk assessment, sustainability principles, and adaptive financial governance are essential to safeguarding asset-backed securities in a warming world. The study concludes that coordinated regulatory reforms, informed by climate science and sustainable finance principles, can improve market stability while supporting the broader transition to a low-carbon economy (Merchant; Mishra et al.; Wang; Westermeier).

title: AI-Based Decision Frameworks for Climate-Adaptive Financing

detail.title: AI-Based Decision Frameworks for Climate-Adaptive Financing
detail.abstract: Climate change has emerged as a systemic risk that increasingly disrupts financial markets, credit systems, and asset-backed financing mechanisms across sectors and geographies (Merchant). Traditional financial decision-making models are largely static and fail to account for the nonlinear, compounding, and uncertain impacts of climate variability (Gupta and Mahapatra). This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI)-based decision frameworks can enhance climate-adaptive financing by integrating predictive intelligence, adaptive learning, and policy responsiveness (Shen et al.). Using a structured synthesis of interdisciplinary literature spanning finance, agriculture, infrastructure, and climate policy, the research identifies key components and performance outcomes of AI-driven financial decision systems (Tamrakar). The findings indicate that adaptive AI frameworks improve risk forecasting accuracy, optimize capital allocation under uncertainty, and strengthen long-term financial resilience (Mueangphaen et al.). Unexpectedly, transparency and explainability emerge as critical determinants of institutional trust, sometimes outweighing predictive performance (Vujko et al.). The study concludes that AI-based decision frameworks represent a necessary evolution in climate-adaptive financing and calls for integrated policy, governance, and ethical safeguards to support scalable implementation (Merchant).

title: Fantasy Sports App Participation and Its Impact on Sports Consumption Among Indian Youth

detail.title: Fantasy Sports App Participation and Its Impact on Sports Consumption Among Indian Youth

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Informed consent was obtained from all participants. The survey was anonymous and participation was voluntary.

detail.abstract: Fantasy sports platforms have changed how young people in India consume and engage with sport, resulting in a shift from passive spectators to active participants who make choices, analyze player statistics, and compete for either monetary or social gain. This study examines the effects of fantasy sports participation on sports consumption behaviors in Indian youth aged 18-25, and how the regulatory ban on real-money fantasy contests, effective in 2025, influenced these consumption behaviors. This study follows a mixed-method explanatory sequential design, integrating quantitative survey data collected from 105 valid respondents with qualitative interviews to capture both statistical and experiential perspectives. During the quantitative phase, a within-subject pre-post design compared self-reported engagement in sport before the ban and after the ban in three areas of interest: hours of watching live matches, OTT subscriptions, and self-rated interest in sport. Analyzing for changes in the self-reported engagement metrics consisted of paired-sample t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, with regression analysis as a way to control for demographics and motivation. Results reveal a significant decline in sports consumption post-ban: average weekly viewing hours fell by 2.3, OTT subscriptions dropped by 0.28, and sports interest decreased by 2.3 points on a 7-point scale (p < 0.001). Qualitative insights confirmed that the absence of monetary incentives and peer competition reduced both motivation and emotional attachment to sports. The findings suggest that fantasy sports act as a behavioral catalyst for sports engagement, amplifying consumption through informational, motivational, and social pathways. The study concludes that while the ban curbed potential gambling risks, it also weakened the broader sports consumption ecosystem. Policymakers should adopt calibrated regulation emphasizing responsible gaming and transparency rather than outright prohibition. The paper contributes empirically grounded evidence to the literature on digital fandom, gamified engagement, and regulatory policy in India's evolving sports economy.

title: The impact of ESG regulations on EU bank’s profitability

detail.title: The impact of ESG regulations on EU bank’s profitability
detail.abstract: ​We examine whether ESG performance is associated with the profitability of listed EU banks in a period of intensified sustainability regulation. Using panel data for 84 banks from 18 EU countries over 2020–2024, we estimate one-way and two-way fixed-effects models with return on assets (ROA) and return on capital employed (ROCE) as profitability measures. We distinguish between the aggregate ESG score and its Environmental, Social, and Governance pillars, while controlling for leverage, bank size, and macroeconomic conditions. The results show that Environmental and Social scores are positively associated with bank profitability, whereas the aggregate ESG score is neutral to negative and Governance is generally insignificant. These findings suggest that aggregate ESG measures may obscure economically relevant heterogeneity across pillars. In the EU banking context, targeted Environmental and Social practices appear more closely linked to profitability than broad ESG engagement, likely because they improve risk management, operational efficiency, and stakeholder confidence, while aggregate scores also capture compliance and disclosure costs. Our results contribute to the ESG–bank performance literature by highlighting the importance of disaggregating ESG measures and by providing evidence from a highly regulated institutional setting. The findings have implications for bank managers, regulators, and investors, supporting a pillar-specific approach to the evaluation of ESG performance.

title: Unsupervised Learning-Based Operational Regime Discovery and Weather Sensitivity Analysis of a Residential Photovoltaic Battery System for Energy Management
affiliations: VSB - Technical University of Ostrava - Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, VSB - Technical University of Ostrava - Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, VSB - Technical University of Ostrava, Technical University Of Crete and VSB - Technical University of Ostrava

detail.title: Unsupervised Learning-Based Operational Regime Discovery and Weather Sensitivity Analysis of a Residential Photovoltaic Battery System for Energy Management
detail.abstract: Behind-the-meter photovoltaic battery systems exhibit heterogeneous daily operating behaviors shaped by weather conditions, household demand, storage control, and grid interaction. Identifying these operational regimes is essential for improving forecasting, system control, and policy design, particularly where labeled operational data are unavailable. This study proposes a fully label-free, unsupervised framework to identify recurring daily operational regimes in a residential photovoltaic battery system and to quantify regime-specific weather sensitivities. Fourteen months of high-resolution operational data from a residential photovoltaic battery system in Yangon, Myanmar, are analyzed. Daily features capturing photovoltaic generation, electricity consumption, grid exchange, battery charging and discharging, state of charge, and self-consumption are derived from intraday profiles. Isolation Forest outlier detection removes anomalous operating days, yielding 411 representative days for analysis. K-means clustering identifies four distinct operational regimes, validated using Gaussian Mixture Models, hierarchical clustering, and density-based methods. Principal component analysis confirms clear separation and interpretability of the identified regimes. Cluster-wise standardized regression models link daily photovoltaic energy production to meteorological drivers. Solar irradiance is the dominant explanatory variable across all regimes, with effect sizes increasing from grid-dependent to self-sufficient operating modes. Temperature and relative humidity exhibit regime-dependent secondary effects, while wind speed plays a limited role. Seasonal analysis reveals systematic shifts in regime prevalence driven by climatic conditions. The proposed framework provides an interpretable and transferable approach for diagnosing real-world photovoltaic battery system behavior and yields actionable regime labels that support regime-aware forecasting and adaptive energy management in distributed energy systems.

title: Unlocking Energy Efficiency and Energy Saving Potentials in Austrian Industry: Firm-Level Evidence from Stochastic Frontier Analysis
affiliations: Oesterreichische Nationalbank (OeNB) and Austrian National Bank

detail.title: Unlocking Energy Efficiency and Energy Saving Potentials in Austrian Industry: Firm-Level Evidence from Stochastic Frontier Analysis
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the drivers of changes in energy intensity and explores energy-saving potentials at the firm level within Austria’s manufacturing and construction sectors from 2008 to 2022. The analysis focuses on the role of energy efficiency. Using firm-level data and applying stochastic frontier analysis, the study reveals that reductions in energy intensity were primarily attributable to scale efficiency gains and technological progress rather than improvements in energy efficiency alone. Despite considerable heterogeneity among firms, counterfactual scenarios with varying ambition levels suggest that raising low-efficiency firms to the median efficiency could yield one-off energy savings of 11.7–13.2%. However, rebound effects would reduce net savings to 8.4–9.7%, corresponding to 12.3–14.2% of the final energy consumption reduction mandated by the Austrian Energy Efficiency Act (EEffG). While these savings are significant, they fall short of offsetting recent energy price shocks and their contribution to the achievement of long-term national and EU policy targets is limited. The findings underscore the need for policy approaches that extend beyond energy-specific measures to also foster productivity, innovation, and structural transformation.

title: Pressure management and energy optimization of district heating systems in high-elevation terrain:A coordinated pump-valve approach
affiliations: Hebei University of Technology, Hebei University of Technology, Hebei University of Technology, Hebei University of Technology, Hebei University of Technology and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Pressure management and energy optimization of district heating systems in high-elevation terrain:A coordinated pump-valve approach
detail.abstract: Central heating systems in mountainous regions face significant hydraulic risks due to large elevation differences, which may cause overpressure in low-lying areas and vaporization at high points. To enhance operational safety and energy efficiency, this study proposes a coordinated pump–valve control system integrated with a near-constant neutral point strategy to maintain hydraulic stability within a predefined safe range. An energy consumption model is established based on load forecasting and pump performance characteristics. An objective function minimizing total operating cost is formulated under multi-parameter constraints, including pressure, temperature, and flow rate. A constraint-aware adaptive population genetic algorithm (CA-APGA) is developed to determine the optimal control strategy. The proposed approach is validated in a real heating project located in a mountainous area. Results show that the neutral point fluctuation range is reduced by 1.13 km and maintained within 0.7–0.9 km. Pressure standard deviation decreases significantly, improving hydraulic stability by 22.22%. The network operating pressure is reduced from 1 MPa to 0.85 MPa while ensuring safety. During the heating season, electricity consumption and heat consumption decrease by 19.23% and 9.85%, respectively. Corresponding carbon emissions from electricity and coal are reduced by 19.23% and 9.85%, and total operating costs decrease by 4.887 million yuan.

title: Waste heat recovery of the glass melting furnace via non-linear process optimization
affiliations: RWTH Aachen University, RWTH Aachen University, RWTH Aachen University, RWTH Aachen University, RWTH Aachen University and Institute of Technical Thermodynamics, RWTH Aachen University

detail.title: Waste heat recovery of the glass melting furnace via non-linear process optimization
detail.abstract: The European glass industry faces strict greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reduction targets, necessitating enhanced energy efficiency in glass melting processes. Enegry efficiency can be enhanced by, e.g., waste heat recovery. This study presents a mathematical optimization model incorporating waste heat recovery (WHR) through multi-stage configurations in glass furnaces. Current practices primarily utilize single-stage WHR, which still results in significant energy losses, particularly from high-temperature flue gases. Our model incorporates five WHR technologies: oxidizer preheating, fuel preheating, batch and cullet preheating, heat-to-power conversion, and integration into a carbon capture process. Our model optimizes both total annualized cost (TAC) and GHG emissions of configurations of WHR technologies for the glass melting furnace in a multi-objective optimization. Our results demonstrate that imple-menting multi-stage WHR can substantially lower both TAC and GHG emissions: A two-stage WHR configuration with air preheating and carbon capture reduces TAC by 31.4% and GHG emissions by 70% compared to using a natural gas-fired glass furnace with air preheating. Furthermore, a sensitivity analysis reveals that while increasing electrification diminishes avail-able waste heat for recovery, optimal multi-stage WHR configurations can still yield significant benefits across different fuel and electrification scenarios. Overall, our research underscores the importance of advanced process modeling and optimization in developing cost-effective strategies for enhancing energy efficiency within the glass industry amidst evolving regulatory landscapes. The findings provide valuable insights for decision-makers aiming to implement economically and environmentally favorable practices in new furnace designs while meeting future emission standards.

title: Opponent Modeling in Incomplete-Information Colonel Blotto Games via a Lossless Payoff-Curve Representation
affiliations: National Key Laboratory for Complex Systems Simulation, National Key Laboratory for Complex Systems Simulation, National Key Laboratory for Complex Systems Simulation, National Key Laboratory for Complex Systems Simulation and National Key Laboratory for Complex Systems Simulation

detail.title: Opponent Modeling in Incomplete-Information Colonel Blotto Games via a Lossless Payoff-Curve Representation

keywords.keywords: Colonel Blotto、incomplete information、opponent modeling 、payoff-curve representation 、exploitability evaluation 、dynamic programming

detail.abstract: We develop a computational framework for exact opponent modeling in incomplete-information competitive resource allocation, with Colonel Blotto games as the canonical setting. Under private budgets, a realized type faces a posterior-weighted family of budget-contingent opponent strategies rather than a single known mixed strategy.Our main result shows that, under battlefield-wise additive and local payoffs, this opponent object admits a lossless type-wise representation by induced payoff curves, one per battlefield. This result is non-trivial: the exact-sum coupling of the feasible set could in principle force dependence on joint cross-battlefield distributional information about the opponent, but we show that under additive and local payoffs this dependence does not materialize---per-battlefield marginals suffice. The representation preserves interim expected utility for every feasible allocation and therefore preserves exact preference comparisons over the original exact-sum feasible set.This representation yields two exact computational consequences. First, the type-wise best-response problem reduces to a deterministic separable exact-sum allocation problem solvable by dynamic programming in pseudo-polynomial time. Second, in constant-sum instances, the same representation supports exact type-wise deviation checking and restricted-game refinement. The payoff-curve oracle provides a unified interface for opponent modeling, exact optimization, and exploitability evaluation: given any opponent strategy and realized budget, it constructs the opponent model, solves for the exact best response, and evaluates exploitability within a single computational pipeline. Computational experiments confirm type dependence of the representation, sensitivity of exact decisions to perturbations, oracle reuse in refinement, and the practical necessity of exact curve construction---showing that approximate opponent models cannot reliably support exact type-wise decision-making regardless of sample size.

title: Exact and Evolutionary Approaches for an Integrated Parallel Machine Tooling Problem with Diameter and Material Setups
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Salento, University of Salento, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Exact and Evolutionary Approaches for an Integrated Parallel Machine Tooling Problem with Diameter and Material Setups
detail.abstract: Efficient management of tool switches is a critical issue in parallel machine environments where setup operations arise from tool loading, diameter adjustments and material changes. While tool loading constraints have been widely studied, the joint consideration of diameter adjustments and material changes has received comparatively limited attention in the scheduling literature. This paper studies an integrated parallel machine tooling problem that incorporates these setup dependencies, reflecting operational conditions observed in manufacturing systems.Two mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulations are developed. Model~1 extends formulations from the literature, while Model~2, inspired by the multiple travelling salesman problem, is designed to capture the problem's combinatorial structure better. Both models solve a relaxed formulation that does not explicitly incorporate unloading decisions, and a final schedule is obtained by applying a KTNS-based policy.Computational experiments show that Model~1 is limited to small instances, whereas Model~2 presents better scalability. However, for some medium- and large-sized instances that meet the imposed time limit, the relaxed solution does not always yield a feasible schedule after the KTNS procedure.In addition, three evolutionary metaheuristic approaches are analysed: a permutation-based genetic algorithm (GA), its memetic extension with bounded local search (GA+LS), and a hybrid biased random-key genetic algorithm (BRKGA). Results on synthetic benchmarks show that BRKGA performs best overall, particularly on larger instances.An industrial case study reveals a different pattern: for medium-sized real instances, GA and GA+LS produce solutions comparable to those of the exact model within substantially shorter runtimes.

title: Revisiting Local Search for Curriculum-Based Course Timetabling
affiliations: University of Udine, University of Udine, University of Udine and University of Udine

detail.title: Revisiting Local Search for Curriculum-Based Course Timetabling
detail.abstract: Curriculum-Based Course Timetabling (CB‐CTT) is a well‐established benchmark problem in educational timetabling, with numerous real and synthetic datasets. Despite its long history of algorithmic developments, designing search methods that work effectively across diverse datasets under time limits remains challenging. In this paper, we focus on local search and, after a thorough analysis of all neighborhood structures reported in the literature, we propose an improved Simulated Annealing (SA) algorithm driven by an extended version of the classic LectureMove neighborhood, called LectureKick, that allows flexible lecture relocation while preserving feasibility. The neighborhood is further enriched with several sampling biases specifically designed to address the soft constraints of CB-CTT, while the overall behavior of the SA is regulated by a cut-off mechanism embedded in the cooling schedule.The method involves numerous parameters, both for the SA schedule and for the neighborhood biases, which are rigorously tuned on a large artificial dataset. The final algorithm is subsequently evaluated on the available benchmarks, including the "standard" ITC~2007 comp dataset, under the original competition timeout conditions.The results show that our approach clearly outperforms all previously proposed local search methods and is competitive with the best methods reported for CB-CTT overall, while improving upon them on several instances.

title: Decision making for wind turbine pitch transmissions based on digital twins accounting for structural integrity
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Mondragon University, Faculty of Engineering, Mondragon Univeristy, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Cantabria

detail.title: Decision making for wind turbine pitch transmissions based on digital twins accounting for structural integrity
detail.abstract: Wear-driven degradation in wind turbine pitch transmissions is governed by the interaction between load magnitude and recurrence, yet conventional lifetime assessments rarely incorporate time-resolved operating conditions. This work presents a physics-based modelling framework that integrates aeroelastic load simulations, local gear contact analysis, and progressive wear prediction within a digital twin environment. The approach accounts for climate scenarios, blade surface degradation, and predictive maintenance strategies. Results for 3.4~MW onshore and 15~MW offshore turbines show that wear is strongly localised on a critical tooth and mainly driven by recurrent intermediate wind speeds. Blade degradation slightly reduces wear accumulation, whereas periodic gear repositioning significantly extends service life. Severe climate scenarios accelerate degradation and shorten predicted lifetime. Overall, the framework supports reliability-oriented decision-making for pitch transmission operation and maintenance.

title: Teachers at the Crossroads: Autonomy, Defensibility, and Self-Efficacy in Preschool Settings
affiliations: Achva Academic College and Achva Academic College

detail.title: Teachers at the Crossroads: Autonomy, Defensibility, and Self-Efficacy in Preschool Settings
detail.abstract: The study introduces two novel concepts for preschool teachers in Israel: Preschool Teachers' Autonomy Perception (PTAP) and Preschool Teachers' Professional Defensibility Perception (PTPPD), and examines their relationship with Professional Self-Efficacy Perception (PSEP), in Israeli educational settings.The research defines teacher autonomy as perceived independence in decision-making, management, emotional development, and pedagogical practices within constraints of limited freedom. Defensibility is conceptualized as teachers' confidence in external influences, shaped by personal beliefs, community perceptions, and the views of Ministry of Education officials.Using a sample of 209 Israeli preschool teachers across various districts, the study employed an anonymous self-report questionnaire with three parts: two newly developed measures and an existing self-efficacy instrument. The analysis used Facet Theory to conceptualize complex phenomena and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) to examine predictive relationships. Model fit indices (RMSEA=0.00, TLI=1.00, CFI=1.00, NFI=0.953) indicated excellent alignment between theoretical and empirical models.Key findings revealed that PTPPD predicts PSEP in parent-child interactions. Paradoxically, high levels of both autonomy and defensibility predicted lower self-efficacy. An inverse relationship emerged between autonomy and defensibility. Background variables, regional affiliation, and job characteristics predicted both autonomy and defensibility levels.The post-COVID-19 data collection context may have influenced the results, as widespread uncertainty may have affected teachers' perceptions. The study's theoretical model offers significant academic and practical implications, contributing to educational policy development, supervision strategies, teacher training curricula, and professional development programs. These insights could enhance teacher self-efficacy, strengthen defensibility and autonomy, and potentially reduce teacher attrition in early childhood education.

title: Techno-economic analysis of olive pomace valorization into phenols and biochar via local centralized and decentralized processing models
affiliations: Virginia Tech, California Polytechnic State University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Virginia Tech, California Polytechnic State University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Virginia Tech and Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University

detail.title: Techno-economic analysis of olive pomace valorization into phenols and biochar via local centralized and decentralized processing models
detail.abstract: Olive pomace is a major by-product of the olive oil industry and it contains abundant value-added compounds such as phenols. Effective valorization of this material can simultaneously reduce environmental burdens and generate high-value bioproducts. However, current techno-economic analysis (TEA) primarily focus on large-scale centralized systems, with limited attention to small-scale or localized production. This study investigates the economic feasibility of olive pomace valorization for small producers through a comparative TEA of two process configurations: (1) a local centralized model, in which multiple nearby olive oil mills cooperatively establish a shared treatment facility, and (2) a decentralized model, where mobile treatment units are employed for on-site processing during the harvest season. The total capital investments (TCI) were estimated at USD 1.93 million and USD 0.33 million for the centralized and decentralized models, respectively. Compared with the decentralized model, which exhibited a negative net present value (NPV) of –0.52M USD, the centralized system demonstrated substantially better economic performance, achieving an NPV of 1.21M USD, an internal rate of return (IRR) of 25.0%, and a payback period of 4.1 years, primarily attributable to its continuous, year-round operation enabled by drying wet pomace during the harvest season. Sensitivity analysis identified phenol product selling price, phenol content in pomace, and phenol extraction efficiency as key determinants of profitability. Overall, the results indicate that cooperative, local centralized processing enables economically viable olive pomace valorization under small-scale and seasonal production constraints, whereas fully decentralized mobile systems are unlikely to be feasible without extended operation or multi-feedstock integration.

title: Improving Iterative Construction Heuristics for Berth Allocation Using Reinforcement Learning
affiliations: University Clermont Auvergne, Mohammed VI Polytechnic University and Mohammed VI Polytechnic University

detail.title: Improving Iterative Construction Heuristics for Berth Allocation Using Reinforcement Learning
detail.abstract: The Continuous Berth Allocation Problem involves assigning incoming vessels to berth positions and service start times along a continuous quay and is known for its computational complexity. In practice, solution methods often rely on iterative construction heuristics, in which vessels are scheduled sequentially using simple decision rules. In particular, berth position selection is commonly handled through ad-hoc greedy policies, despite its impact on overall solution quality. This work explores the integration of reinforcement learning into iterative constructors for the continuous berth allocation problem. A sequential construction policy is proposed that combines a deterministic earliest-feasible start time rule with a reinforcement learning–based berth position selection mechanism. The learning problem is formulated as a Markov decision process and solved using a Prioritized Double Deep Q-Network. The proposed approach is evaluated on statistically generated instances under two terminal configurations. Numerical results show that the learning-based constructor significantly improves solution quality in congested environments while remaining competitive in less constrained settings. These findings illustrate the potential of reinforcement learning to enhance constructive heuristics for berth allocation.

title: FlowPrioritize: A Model-Driven Priority Scheduling Library for Asynchronous Rust Runtimes
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: FlowPrioritize: A Model-Driven Priority Scheduling Library for Asynchronous Rust Runtimes
detail.abstract: Modern online multiplayer games and real-time distributed APIs inherently process highly heterogeneous workloads. Small-sized, frequent data packets (mouse flows) responsible for critical state synchronization constantly compete for compute resources against infrequent but throughput-heavy tasks (elephant flows), such as database persistence. Traditional First-In-First-Out (FIFO) queueing strategies inevitably cause mouse flows to suffer from severe head-of-line blocking during traffic bursts. To resolve this, we present FlowPrioritize, an open-source Rust library built on the Tokio asynchronous runtime. It abstracts mixed-workload processing as a formal M/M/c priority queue. The software incorporates a zero-cost telemetry thread to calculate the Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) of arrival and service rates, thereby estimating the real-time system load (rho). Based on rho, it dynamically applies non-preemptive strict priority to protect sub-millisecond tail latency for mouse flows, and enforces an active admission control mechanism during overloads to prevent system collapse.

title: Balance or Combination? How Executive Innovation Cognition Shapes Ambidextrous Technological Innovation in Manufacturing Firms
affiliations: Hohai University and Shanghai Lixin University of Accounting and Finance

detail.title: Balance or Combination? How Executive Innovation Cognition Shapes Ambidextrous Technological Innovation in Manufacturing Firms
detail.abstract: Adopting an appropriate ambidextrous technological innovation model is crucial for manufacturing enterprises to build sustainable competitive advantages. However, most existing studies adopt a static analytical framework and fail to reveal the dynamic adaptation law of innovation models with the enterprise's development stages. Integrating management cognition theory and the corporate life cycle theory, this study systematically examines the impact and mechanism of executive innovation cognition on ambidextrous balanced and combined technological innovation, based on data from Chinese Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share manufacturing enterprises during 2010-2022. The results show that executive innovation cognition has a significantly positive promoting effect on both types of ambidextrous technological innovation, but this effect exhibits distinct life cycle heterogeneity. Further research finds that university-industry-research collaboration plays a mediating role between executive innovation cognition and the two types of ambidextrous technological innovation, and this mediating effect is more significant for ambidextrous combined technological innovation only in declining-stage enterprises. This study deeply integrates the corporate life cycle perspective into ambidextrous innovation research, reveals the dynamic adaptation logic between executive innovation cognition and ambidextrous technological innovation, and fills the gap in existing studies regarding insufficient attention to the phased management of ambidextrous innovation. Meanwhile, it expands the cross-application boundary of management cognition theory and corporate life cycle theory, providing practical basis for manufacturing enterprises to adjust their technological innovation models according to their development stages.

title: A Multi-timescale DRL-DRO MPC Framework for Microgrid Scheduling Under Prediction Uncertainty
affiliations: Guangzhou University, Guangzhou University, Guangzhou University, Guangzhou University, Guangzhou University and Guangzhou University

detail.title: A Multi-timescale DRL-DRO MPC Framework for Microgrid Scheduling Under Prediction Uncertainty
detail.abstract: AbstractWith the continuous increase in the penetration rate of renewable energy, the intermittency and uncertainty of its output pose serious challenges to the safe and stable operation and economic dispatch of microgrids. Traditional deterministic scheduling methods struggle to effectively manage fluctuations in renewable energy and load demand. A novel three-layer coupled microgrid scheduling framework based on Model Predictive Control (MPC) is proposed to address the uncertainty of renewable energy and improve the economic and operational efficiency of microgrids, and it is optimized using Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO) that integrates Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). In the day-ahead scheduling layer, K-means clustering/Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) are employed to preprocess complex historical data of renewable energy output and load. A hybrid prediction model integrating self-attention (SA), bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM), and residual learning correction is then developed, where adaptive quantile regression (AQR) is introduced to generate uncertainty prediction sets and subjected to distributionally robust optimization to derive robust day-ahead schedules. Subsequently, in the intraday optimization layer, rolling optimization is performed based on updated ultra-short-term forecasts to refine day-ahead plans. Then, in the intraday real-time correlation layer, MPC-based fast-rolling optimization is implemented to track renewable energy fluctuations in real time and maintain system power balance. Finally, comparative economic analysis, rolling scheduling evaluations, and control performance experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework not only significantly improves microgrid economics (4.1%) but also substantially enhances system controllability and robustness (7.4%) against uncertainties.

title: Bi-level Optimal Scheduling of a Multi-Energy Microgrid Integrated Energy System Considering Dynamic Carbon Emission Allowance Allocation and CET-GCT Coordination
affiliations: North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University and North China Electric Power University

detail.title: Bi-level Optimal Scheduling of a Multi-Energy Microgrid Integrated Energy System Considering Dynamic Carbon Emission Allowance Allocation and CET-GCT Coordination
detail.abstract: As the energy crisis and environmental challenges intensify, integrated energy systems (IESs) and multi-energy microgrids (MMGs) have attracted growing attention due to their multi-energy coordination capability and low-carbon potential. However, under current coordinated scheduling frameworks for IESs and MMGs, existing CET mechanisms cannot dynamically reflect real-time emission disparities among different entities. As a result, carbon emission allowances (CEAs) are underutilized, which consequently weakens the effectiveness of low-carbon dispatch. Meanwhile, the synergistic effects of low-carbon dispatch mechanisms, such as carbon emissions trading (CET) and green certificate trading (GCT), have not been fully exploited. To address these issues, this paper proposed a bi-level scheduling method for an IES that considered dynamic CEA allocation and coordination between the carbon and green certificate markets. First, an interconnected model of an IES with multiple MMGs was established. Based on carbon emission flow theory, the nodal carbon footprint (NCF) was computed in real time from nodal carbon intensity, and dynamic CEA allocation was performed by incorporating the Shapley value method. For lower-level users, MMGs were allowed to choose, under prevailing allowance intervals, whether to sell green certificates or to offset carbon emissions. Also, MMGs could conduct carbon emission allowance trading (CEAT) among themselves, thereby leveraging the synergistic benefits of the two mechanisms. Compared with traditional models, the proposed method further unlocked emission-reduction potential while maintaining system economic efficiency. The simulation results demonstrated that the total system cost decreased by 11.68% and total carbon emissions decreased by 4.43%.

title: Predictive and Reserve-Aware Online Orchestration of 5G Network Slices for URLLC
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Predictive and Reserve-Aware Online Orchestration of 5G Network Slices for URLLC
detail.abstract: Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communications (URLLC) imposes stringent latency and reliability requirements that are difficult to sustain in dynamic 5G network slicing environments, especially under demand uncertainty and abrupt traffic surges. This paper proposes PRISM-URLLC (Predictive and Reserve-aware Slice Management for URLLC), a prediction-integrated and reserve-aware online slice orchestration framework for URLLC-oriented resource allocation under dynamic multi-slice conditions. The proposed method combines observed demand, short-horizon predicted demand, QoS sensitivity, slice priority, and urgency-related signals within a lightweight score-based allocation mechanism. To improve responsiveness under sudden load escalation, the framework further introduces an uncertainty-aware adaptive emergency reservation policy that adjusts the reserved resource budget according to urgency intensity, predicted URLLC demand, and prediction uncertainty. Rather than relying on a specific forecasting architecture, PRISM-URLLC is designed to incorporate predictive inputs in a modular manner while preserving low computational overhead. The framework is evaluated in an abstract slice-level 5G simulation environment under nominal, high-load, and emergency-surge traffic regimes, and is compared against demand-aware, priority-based, fairness-oriented, and hybrid non-predictive baselines under identical assumptions. Results show that the proposed method improves URLLC-oriented service indicators, including demand satisfaction and latency-related performance proxies, particularly under high-load and emergency-surge conditions, while maintaining competitive fairness, resource utilization, and runtime efficiency. Additional analyses on scalability, robustness to prediction noise, and component ablation further support the relevance of the proposed framework as a practical online orchestration mechanism for dynamic URLLC-oriented slice management.

title: Towards fairer public transit: Real-time tensor fusionof video and audio for fare evasion and fraud detection
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority

detail.title: Towards fairer public transit: Real-time tensor fusionof video and audio for fare evasion and fraud detection
detail.abstract: This study developed a real-time multimodal system to detect fare evasionand fraud in public transportation by integrating video and audio streamsfrom CCTV. The system addressed the limitations of manual surveillancecurrently used in Rwanda, where fare enforcement is highly dependent onoperators monitoring multiple camera feeds simultaneously. To capture com-plex behavioral and acoustic indicators of fraud, we employed the VisionTransformer for Video (ViViT) for spatio-temporal video feature extractionand the Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST) for transaction-related au-dio analysis. A Tensor Fusion Network (TFN) was adapted and extendedto explicitly model unimodal and bimodal interactions between visual andaudio modalities through a 2-fold Cartesian product. The model was trainedand evaluated on a custom dataset of 820 synchronized video–audio sam-ples, representing real-world boarding scenarios labeled as either legitimateor fraudulent. Using a stratified 5-fold cross-validation procedure, the sys-tem achieved an accuracy of 89.5%, a precision of 87.2%, a recall of 84.0%,and an F1-score of 85.6%, outperforming both unimodal baselines and earlyand latefusion methods. Ablation studies further demonstrated that explicittensor fusion improved the F1-score by 7.0% over traditional concatenationapproaches. These results highlight the potential of multimodal tensor-basedlearning to significantly improve automation, reduce revenue leakage, and im-prove operational compliance in public transportation systems. The findingsprovide a foundation for scalable deployment and motivate future work onintegrating additional data sources, increasing the size of the dataset, andimproving the robustness under real-world conditions.

title: Robust Reinforcement Learning for Market Making under Regime Uncertainty: Numerical Evidence from Multi-Regime Training
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Robust Reinforcement Learning for Market Making under Regime Uncertainty: Numerical Evidence from Multi-Regime Training
detail.abstract: Recent studies on reinforcement-learning-based market making have advanced policy expressiveness, robust training, and the realism of simulation environments. Nevertheless, one fundamental question has not yet been directly verified: when market conditions vary across regimes, can a policy trained on a broader distribution of seen markets exhibit stronger out-of-sample robustness on unseen regimes? In a model-based limit order book environment, this paper formulates the market-making problem as a finite-horizon Markov decision process parameterized by the regime vector m = (σ, A, k), and compares single-regime training with multi-regime random-sampling training under a unified reward specification and identical PPO hyperparameters. Return-side robustness is primarily evaluated by Mean PnL, CVaR10%, and CVaR30%, with the mean and variance of terminal inventory reported as diagnostic indicators. The results show that, in both the interpolation-type unseen market U1 and the stress-type unseen market U2, Multi-PPO achieves higher average returns and better lower-tail risk metrics than the two single-regime baselines. In the stress market, kernel density estimation and empirical cumulative distribution functions further indicate that Multi-PPO weakens the left-tail mass of the return distribution and lowers the probability of poor outcomes. These findings suggest that enlarging the support of the training distribution helps reduce the sensitivity of the policy to regime mismatch, thereby improving return-side robustness in unseen markets. At the same time, the variance of terminal inventory does not decrease in parallel, indicating that the improvement in returns remains accompanied by a trade-off in inventory fluctuations.
